chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abū ʿUbaydah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who sees purity while she is traveling, and she does not have with her enough water to suffice for her ghusl, while the time of salat has arrived. He said: “If she has with her enough for washing her private part, then she should wash it, then perform tayammum, and pray.” I said: Then may her husband approach her in that state? He said: “Yes, if she has washed her private part and performed tayammum.”

key_terms.تَتَيَمَّمُ: she performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.غُسْلِهَا: her ritual bath required after menstruation
key_terms.فَرْجَهَا: her private part, to be washed with the available water
key_terms.ٱلطُّهْرَ: the state of becoming pure from menstruation

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do if her menstruation ends during travel and she does not have enough water for ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a menstruating woman who becomes pure during travel but lacks sufficient water for ghusl. She is instructed to wash her private part with the available water, perform tayammum, and offer salat; in that state, marital relations are also permitted after washing and tayammum.
